GeoCoreServer._comment: XD01-382: the kernel's ROOT URL (no /api/geoassets suffix). Features, the global target ledger, the order-type registry, the permission contributor endpoint and the caller's identity are all reached over the kernel's REST API under it.

ServiceAuth._comment: XD01-299: client credentials of this host's GeoAssets.ServiceCaller service principal. Disabled (the default) registers no token provider: the kernel's machine-to-machine routes then answer 401, the vertical-registration check stays Degraded (/healthz still 200, /readyz 503) and ledger reservations answer 503. Tokens are asked from Instance + TenantId (XD01-452; blank Instance = AzureAdCiam:Instance): the kernel accepts only its CIAM instance's issuer, never a login.microsoftonline.com token.

VerticalRegistration._comment: XD01-382: retry schedule of the bootstrap registration (exponential backoff with jitter from InitialDelay to MaxDelay until it succeeds), then republished every RefreshInterval.

AzureAdCiam._comment: ClientId is this host's own API registration (XD01-390, CIAM model (b): one app registration per API, and the Web/MAUI clients request its scope for this vertical's routes). This host forwards the caller's own token to the kernel's identity routes (/api/identity/me, /api/identity/policies, /api/identity/organization-grants/me), so the kernel must accept this audience: list it in the kernel's AzureAdCiam:AdditionalAudiences (AzureAdCiam__AdditionalAudiences__1=<this ClientId or its App ID URI>). The Web/MAUI clients request this API's scope for /api/v/neutral-operator/ once their GeoAssetsServer:RouteScopes entry names it (XD01-397), so model (b) works end to end. Alternatively (model (a)) use the kernel's API audience here and leave the clients' route scope blank. A kernel that rejects the token answers 502 kernel.token-rejected.

GeoAssets._comment: GeoAssets:Modules (XD01-382): this host's modules; 'neutral-operator' is the vertical itself.

Outbox._comment: Workflow integration-event transport (XD01-357): 'Kafka' (options in 'WorkflowKafka'), 'ServiceBus' (options in 'WorkflowServiceBus') or 'None'. With a broker, every order status change stages OrderStateChangedV1 (VerticalId neutral-operator) for the kernel's target-ledger consumer, and the approval saga (XD01-383) runs: approvals stage AssetMutationBatchRequestedV1 for the kernel and this host consumes its AppliedV1/RejectedV1 replies from the consumer topic (WorkflowKafkaConsumer:TopicName, groups {GroupId}.OccupancyApplySagaApplied / .OccupancyApplySagaRejected unless WorkflowKafkaConsumer:Consumers:{key}:GroupId says otherwise; Service Bus: WorkflowServiceBusConsumer:Consumers:{key}:SubscriptionName). With 'None' everything staged stays pending — the saga needs a broker on this host (a startup warning says so): approvals stay 'awaiting apply' and time out.

Saga._comment: XD01-383: an approval still awaiting the kernel's apply ApplyTimeout after its batch was last staged is flagged (geoassets.saga.apply.timeouts, a structured warning; alert rules in deploy/otel/alerts) and stays pending; POST /api/workflow/service-orders/{id}/occupancy-saga/retry stages it again.
